Study at review (960x412, 1152 frames): 23 of 23 gates pass, seam step 0.965 and seam acceleration 0.993 against 1.1, motion-in value over floor clouds 1.043e-3/2.37e-4, mist 7.44e-4/2.83e-4, pool-steam 9.78e-4/2.16e-4, wisps 3.16e-4/2.41e-4; at smoke the mist margin was 6 % and the wisps margin 21 %. Hot-pool digest unchanged.

Re-runs after the four rebases that followed #55's opening (measured): after the seam-floor change, fast 221 passed, 1 skipped, slow 36 passed, repo tests 762; after EC-3's rain, c01, c02, c09, c10, c11 and c12 24 passed, repo tests 808; after EC-4's fire, c08, c10 and c11 8 passed. The full fast, slow and budget tiers were not rerun after the EC-3 and EC-4 rebases (the worker's estimate: low risk, those commits add new files and a glass-layer rule none of EC-2's layers uses). Forge CI on d3e8bd9: success, 5 min 53 s.

Rework, PR #70 (measured, from the PR body): fast 221 passed, 1 skipped (c06, by design), 814 s; slow 36 passed; budget 2 passed; repo tests 1021, then 1106 after the rebase onto c38b136; c01, c08, c10 and c11 11 passed after the rebase with the review package rebuilt; all 1152 master frame hashes equal before and after the rebase and 23 of 23 gates in both packages (the code digest moved with main, the pixels did not). Study at review: seam step 0.966, seam acceleration 0.991; motion-in clouds 7.2e-4, mist 9.5e-4, pool-steam 1.33e-3, wisps 7.5e-4 (floors 2.2e-4, 2.9e-4, 2.2e-4, 2.5e-4); at smoke the mist margin is 28 %, from 6 %, and the wisps margin 140 %. Hot-pool digest unchanged. The worker states no content was shaped for a statistic and no exemption was asked.

Look. Wave-1 independent picture review (Opus, frames and measurements): clouds ship with notes, mist ship with notes, steam@2 needs rework (scene maps only). Re-check of the seven repairs by a second Opus reviewer that wrote none of the code or maps, told not to read the author's record first: no blocker; highlight churn (mean step 3.5x the rest of the sky to 1.06x), forest drag (pines temporal std 1.50 to 0.03) and steam occlusion fixed; scud, mist and steam warmth improved with limits; front wisps only marginally better. It found one defect the rework introduced, the dark scud ending on a line above the bright horizon at x 740 to 840 (clouds region edge fell within about 4 px); the repair widened the ramp (steepest step 5.65 to 1.40 levels per px, map only) and the same reviewer checked it on new frames: no blocker.

Criterion 7 budget, signed off by the coordinator (main 70ae9a4, 2026-11-23 18:34Z, load 5.0 to 8.3 on 16 CPUs; measured), seconds per frame: at review clouds 0.019, mist 0.030, pool-steam 0.015, wisps 0.012; at 3440 clouds 0.217, mist 0.411, pool-steam 0.149, wisps 0.235. The budget limits are in the criteria and are not restated here.
acceptance.note: PR #55 merged fast-forward at d3e8bd9 (2026-11-22 about 18:47Z), one PR for the whole outcome after two rebases before it and four after it; its body carries the first run's numbers because the Forgejo token cannot edit PR bodies. PR #70 merged fast-forward at 70ae9a4 on 2026-11-23 with verify green on the head (merge time not recorded here); it was released on the condition that main held EC-5's c38b136, then rebased and rerun. Until #70 merged, main's atmospherics.yaml failed validation, because EC-0's outdoor-mask merge changed the sky.png and pool-cut digests the study declares; #70 declares the new ones and authors clouds-region, mist-region and mist-warp again on the new sky. Recorded limits after the rework: mist keeps 63 % of the painting's fine detail (from 53 %) and reads as haze more than as banks; the scud's left third is about 30 % weaker and is now the stillest part of the sky; the front wisps are barely there on the figure; clouds near the horizon move less (the horizon band's motion halved); nobody has seen playback or mist and steam at display size. Unchanged from #55: steam@2 is about equal in presence to steam@1; the clouds rim behind the arch is weakened, not frozen; castle spires shimmer about 2 px; the mist region has a straight left edge near x 270; no oracle bounds mist density speed (parked by the coordinator). Disclosure from #55: restricting the mist's painted warp to haze removed most of what motion-in:mist measured, and the worker raised the study's mist flow and wisps density with the gate's numbers in view. Follow-ups left for the human review, whose decision is null: vertical falloff on the mist banks with a darker veil, more density in the front wisps, and the playback and display-size looks. EC-2 asset findings, if any, join EC-0's deferred asset pass.

reviewer.evidence: Original review of #55: one Opus 5.5 subagent (general-purpose, model opus), read-only, resumed twice; it read the diff, the criteria and the plan and looked at rendered frames. Three rounds: 190,664, 238,552 and 253,892 tokens, 105 tool uses, 20.2 min of reviewer wall time (reported; whether the token figures are per run or cumulative is unknown). Round 1 gave 0 blocking, 3 major, 9 minor; round 2 1 major, 3 minor; round 3 0 major, 3 minor ('let it go to the human review'). Its four majors were a 16 s steam repeat, a mist warp that doubled the waterfall, a pool steam sheet over the bather and a hard edge at each vent; all were look defects that every gate and acceptance test had passed. The wave-1 picture review and the rework re-check were Opus reviewers whose model ids and finding severities were not recorded (not counted); the re-check found no blocker. No reviewer changed files.

practice_observation: The independent reviewer found four look defects (a 16 s steam repeat, a doubled waterfall, a steam sheet over the bather, hard vent edges) that all gates and acceptance tests had passed, and the wave-1 picture review then asked for a map-only rework; the re-check of that rework found a hard scud line the rework itself had introduced, so reviewing the repair before merge caught a regression. The visible-motion gate and the painted warp pulled against each other (masking the warp to haze cut motion-in:mist below its floor and the worker met it by raising flow and loosening the mask with the numbers in view, disclosed); a gate for a layer whose job is to be still over structure would be cleaner. Costs: merging into a busy main behind a one-job CI runner took about 4 h and four rebases after #55 opened (estimate), acceptance runs on a loaded box were slow and made s08 skip, and main's study failed validation between EC-0's mask merge and #70. The card routed Terra and a Sonnet session delivered, so this does not test Terra.
